suspected_mouse_proxy: unknown — model should predict (likely Cd28 with altered memory-T expression context; proxy may involve ICOS-like costimulator module)
translational_failure_evidence: In the 2006 TGN1412 cytokine-storm disaster, mouse and macaque Cd28 is not expressed on CD4+ effector memory T cells (unlike human CD28), so preclinical safety testing could not detect the cytokine release mechanism driven by effector-memory CD28 engagement.

suspected_mouse_proxy: unknown — model should predict (no mouse ortholog; functional analog likely resides in PLTP or reverse-cholesterol module)
translational_failure_evidence: CETP is present in humans, rabbits and hamsters but entirely absent from the mouse genome, forcing CETP-transgenic or hamster models and contributing to the translational opacity of the CETP-inhibitor class (torcetrapib death signal, discontinued anacetrapib).

suspected_mouse_proxy: Tnfrsf10b (mouse Killer/DR5 — the single mouse TRAIL death receptor)
translational_failure_evidence: Mice have only one TRAIL death receptor (mKiller/DR5) whereas humans have two (TNFRSF10A/DR4 and TNFRSF10B/DR5); DR4-selective agonist antibodies such as mapatumumab could not be pharmacologically evaluated in wild-type mouse models, and the entire TRAIL-receptor agonist class subsequently failed in clinic.

suspected_mouse_proxy: P2rx7 (mouse ortholog) with known ~5-10× reduced agonist affinity and distinct antagonist pharmacology
translational_failure_evidence: Recombinant mouse P2X7 has ~5-10x lower affinity for ATP/BzATP than human P2X7 and a strikingly different antagonist profile; several P2X7 antagonist programs showed strong rodent efficacy but reached clinic with unclear translation.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Bdkrb1 (with inverted agonist selectivity — mouse B1R prefers des-Arg9-BK whereas human prefers des-Arg10-kallidin ~2000-fold)
translational_failure_evidence: The mouse B1 bradykinin receptor has the opposite agonist selectivity to the human receptor (2-3-fold preference for des-Arg9-BK vs ~2000-fold preference for des-Arg10-kallidin in human), which contributed to the discordance between robust rodent analgesic signals and negative human pain trials.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Ccr5 (mouse ortholog, but >1400-fold lower maraviroc affinity)
translational_failure_evidence: Maraviroc has at least 1400-fold lower affinity for mouse CCR5 than human CCR5 despite ~82% protein identity; small-molecule CCR5 antagonists could not be pharmacologically characterized in mouse and required macaque preclinical models.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Il6r (mouse ortholog — but tocilizumab epitope is not conserved; mouse IL6R signals through a non-conserved site-I interface)
translational_failure_evidence: Tocilizumab completely fails to block mouse IL-6R because the site-I binding interface is not conserved between species; all preclinical efficacy work on IL-6R biologics required a humanized IL6R knock-in mouse.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Pcsk9 (ortholog) — evolocumab binds mouse Pcsk9 ~1000× weaker (KD 17 nM human vs 17000 nM mouse)
translational_failure_evidence: Evolocumab has 1000-fold lower affinity for mouse PCSK9 (17 nM human vs 17000 nM mouse); preclinical efficacy testing required hPCSK9-knock-in mice because wild-type mouse models are functionally blind to the antibody.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Fcgrt (ortholog) with reversed IgG cross-species binding — mouse FcRn binds human IgG1 with ~10× higher affinity than human FcRn
translational_failure_evidence: Human FcRn ignores mouse IgG1 while mouse FcRn binds human IgG1 ~10-fold tighter than human FcRn; the asymmetric cross-species binding distorts preclinical half-life and dosing predictions for all anti-FcRn biologics and Fc-engineered therapeutics.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Scn9a (ortholog) — but divergent tissue expression (strong hypothalamus/adrenal in rodent, absent in primate/human)
translational_failure_evidence: Nav1.7 is expressed in paraventricular/supraoptic hypothalamus and adrenal/pituitary in rodents but is essentially absent from the same primate/human tissues, contributing to lethal neonatal phenotype of mouse KOs and the systematic failure of Nav1.7-selective blockers to translate from rodent pain assays to clinical analgesia.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Cyp3a11 / Cyp3a-cluster (8+ paralogs) — broader and partially divergent substrate spectrum
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse has ~34 Cyp genes in the 1a/2c/2d/3a subfamilies vs 8 functional human ones; CYP3A4 substrate predictions are unreliable in wild-type mice and the 8HUM humanized mouse line was built specifically to rescue preclinical DMPK translation.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Cyp2d cluster (Cyp2d9/10/11/22/26/34/40) — expanded and with different substrate specificity
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse lacks a single functional CYP2D6 equivalent; instead it has an expanded Cyp2d cluster with organ-distribution differences, and CYP2D6-humanized mouse lines must be used to predict CYP2D6-mediated metabolism and polymorphism effects.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Hcar2 (ortholog) — reduced niacin sensitivity and β-arrestin-biased flushing in mouse
translational_failure_evidence: Rodent HCAR2 has reduced sensitivity to niacin compared to human and the flushing response is β-arrestin-biased in mouse vs G-protein-biased in human, contributing to misleading predictions of HDL efficacy and flushing tolerability (MK-1903 and related GPR109A agonists failed).

suspected_mouse_proxy: Cd33 (ortholog) — but binds different sialoglycans and expresses on peripheral granulocytes not myeloid progenitors
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse CD33 does not bind α2-3 or α2-6-linked sialic acids on lactosamine that human CD33 recognizes, and is expressed primarily on mature granulocytes rather than myeloid progenitors, making wild-type mice unsuitable for evaluating CD33-targeted ADCs.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Adrb3 (ortholog) — and species-specific signaling via Adrb3a/Adrb3b splice variants
translational_failure_evidence: Mirabegron and other β3-agonists show higher affinity for human than rodent ADRB3; β3-AR has a uniquely species-dependent ligand recognition profile including low propranolol affinity and different signaling bias between mouse and human.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Havcr2 (ortholog) with divergent ligand engagement — galectin-9 is an established TIM-3 ligand in mouse but not in human
translational_failure_evidence: Galectin-9 serves as a functional TIM-3 ligand in mouse T-cell inhibition but does not bind/activate human TIM-3 in comparable assays; preclinical TIM-3 checkpoint biology in mouse therefore relies on a ligand axis that is not operational in patients.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Tslp (ortholog) — but divergent target-cell biology (mouse TSLP drives B-cell growth; human TSLP drives myeloid/DC activation)
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse TSLP was discovered as a B-cell growth factor whereas human TSLP preferentially stimulates myeloid cells/DCs; tezepelumab development required dual humanized TSLP/TSLPR knock-in mice to recapitulate human allergic airway biology.

suspected_mouse_proxy: C5 (ortholog) — but eculizumab does not bind mouse/rat/rabbit/guinea-pig C5
translational_failure_evidence: Eculizumab is highly species-restricted: no activity against mouse, rat, guinea pig, or rabbit complement, forcing non-orthologous surrogate antibodies (BB5.1) for mouse-based mechanistic studies of the PNH/aHUS axis.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Tigit (ortholog) — but ligand repertoire is reduced; mouse Tigit binds only mPVR (not Nectin-4)
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse TIGIT interacts only with PVR, whereas human TIGIT engages PVR, Nectin-2, Nectin-3 and Nectin-4; several ligand-specific biologies of TIGIT (e.g. Nectin-4 in bladder/tumor contexts) cannot be modeled in wild-type mice, which may contribute to TIGIT class translational setbacks (SKYSCRAPER-01).

suspected_mouse_proxy: Bace1 (ortholog) with added Bace2 off-target context
translational_failure_evidence: Preclinical BACE1 inhibitor studies in mice predicted CNS Aβ reduction but failed to anticipate the human cognitive worsening observed in EPOCH/APECS; off-target BACE2 inhibition (hair depigmentation) and species-divergent LTP effects in mouse hippocampus (worse than KO) illustrate a poorly transferable BACE1 biology.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Nod2 (ortholog) — but Crohn's-risk alleles act in opposite direction in mouse vs human (gain of NF-kB in mouse knock-in vs loss-of-function in human)
translational_failure_evidence: The L1007fsinsC / 3020insC Crohn's-risk NOD2 allele behaves as a loss-of-function in human PBMCs (fail to respond to MDP) yet the equivalent knock-in mouse shows elevated NF-kB and IL-1β processing, inverting the inferred drug-target direction between species.

drug_example: CpG ODN classes (e.g. tilsotolimod, SD-101, agatolimod)
suspected_mouse_proxy: Tlr9 (ortholog) — but optimal CpG motif differs (human GTCGTT vs mouse GACGTT)
translational_failure_evidence: Human TLR9 has a distinct optimal CpG motif (GTCGTT) from mouse (GACGTT); CpG-based immunotherapeutics optimized in mouse models often show reduced human activity, and vice versa, necessitating species-specific motif tuning.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Klrg1 (ortholog) — but mouse KLRG1 forms monomers/oligomers while human forms dimers, with reduced inhibitory function
translational_failure_evidence: Mouse Klrg1 is less inhibitory than human KLRG1 due to a single amino-acid difference at position 62 of the stalk driving monomer/oligomer vs dimer formation; checkpoint blockade of KLRG1 can therefore appear underpowered in mouse compared with anticipated human activity.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Ms4a1 (Cd20 ortholog) — but rituximab epitope on the large extracellular loop is not conserved
translational_failure_evidence: Rituximab is a chimeric anti-human-CD20 that does not recognize mouse CD20 because the critical large-loop epitope is not conserved; all mechanistic B-cell-depletion studies require humanized hCD20 knock-in mice or surrogate mouse anti-CD20 antibodies.

suspected_mouse_proxy: Lep (ortholog) — but human leptin has species-specific Trp100 reducing solubility and altered receptor engagement
translational_failure_evidence: Human leptin differs at a solvent-exposed Trp100 (hominoid-specific) vs mouse Lep, leading to ~20-fold lower solubility and different pharmacokinetics; the ob/ob mouse mutation is rare in humans and extrapolation of leptin/LEPR biology to human obesity has largely failed.
